title: Does steering activations off-manifold leave a detectable fingerprint?

original_idea.body: Fit a density/distance model on clean activations and test whether off-manifold distance predicts both steering failure and probe-detectability.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Dual-use off-manifold monitor is plausible safety infra but the catastrophic-risk chain is moderate/indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Mahalanobis/kNN distance on activations + steering sweep is guided; novice + mentor feasible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable but tests two predictions (failure + detectability) with a fitted density model.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Training-free detector, public model, no internal access; externally doable, lab-deprioritized.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference + cheap distance computations on one model; single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Operationalizing off-manifold distance as a dual-use failure+injection detector appears largely novel.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Turning the off-manifold hypothesis into a measurable dual-use detector is an underexplored operationalization.
